text:
incident-bot: [P1] Latency SLO breach detected in us-east-1 GPU pool. p99 for streaming endpoints ↑ 3.8s (SLO 2.0s). Impacted routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat. Alert rule: streaming_tail_p99 > 2s for 3m. Pager: https://pager.redwood/incident/3141592654 :rotating_light:

anna: i'm on call, grabbing context. tagging infra and ml. @raj @kevin can you take a look at node health and recent deploys?

raj: looking. no deploys in last 15m from deploy-bot. checking node-level metrics now.

kevin: on standby. if it's a streaming stall likely KV cache or GPU stall. will check `nvidia-smi` and driver logs.

sre-bot: autometrics snapshot attached -> short link: https://grafana.redwood/s/alerts/3141592654 (p95 0.9s, p99 3.8s, tail error rate 0.6%).

ops_lead: customer impact: one enterprise tenant reported timeouts on interactive chat. CS notified — @customer-success please confirm.

customer-success: confirmed. customer saw 504s for long-running streams ~07:09-07:18 UTC. They routed around but want RCA.

raj: quick summary from node group us-east-1-gpu-pool:
- 12 nodes total
- 3 nodes showing elevated correctable ECC counts over last 6h
- two nodes with GPU memory spikes coincident with streaming sessions

kevin: SSHing into candidate node `gpu-node-13` (one with highest ECC counts).

kevin: `ssh core@gpu-node-13`
kevin: running `nvidia-smi -q` -> output snippet:
```
==============NVSMI LOG==============
GPU 0:
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp                       : 82 C
    ECC Errors
        Volatile
            Single Bit ECC                    : 423 Corrected
            Double Bit ECC                    : 0 Uncorrected
    Clocks
        Graphics                          : 1380 MHz
    Performance State                   : P0
    Compute Mode                        : Default

Driver warnings: thermal policy invoked, minor throttle events in last 10m
```

anna: 82C and high correctable ECCs — that matches flaky hardware causing occasional stalls. what do we want to do?

kevin: recommend isolating node, draining workloads, and failing over streaming sessions to the rest of the pool. also enable fallback routing to `cpu-fallback-quantized` for long-running streams if available.

sre-bot: issuing cordon/drain operations.

sre-bot: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-13 && kubectl drain gpu-node-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

sre-bot: drain started, evicting 38 pods (streaming pods have session-preserving handoff).

jess: started graceful session handoff for live streams. using prefix KV migration and session replay to avoid user interruption. progress 40% after 30s.

matt: temporarily increased pool autoscale min to +2 to absorb.
matt: `PATCH /api/v1/pools/us-east-1-gpu-pool {"min_nodes":14}`

devex: rerouting rule applied to avoid gpu-node-13 but keep pool online: `routing policy: avoid_node(gpu-node-13)`

raj: also seeing `nvidia-driver` kernel logs with periodic `gpu reset` events synchronized with p99 spikes. snippet:
```
Mar 15 07:10:12 gpu-node-13 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 07:10:15 gpu-node-13 kernel: NVRM: GPU has been reset
```

kevin: that explains stalls — driver resets cause streaming stalls while session state is rebuilt. hardware may be flaky/thermally compromised.

anna: current mitigations in flight:
- isolate & drain gpu-node-13 (in progress)
- increase autoscale to absorb
- enable route fallback to quantized CPU model for any sessions that exceed 2s queue time
- notify customer with interim status

customer-success: emailed customer at 07:21 UTC with interim notice and mitigation steps.

sre-bot: drain complete, node cordoned. Evicted pods redistributed.

raj: traffic redistributed. checking p99 now.

sre-bot: metrics update in 60s...

(1m)

sre-bot: p99 dropped to 1.85s, p95 0.85s. error rate back to baseline.

matt: spinning a replacement node request to infra pool; flagged for hardware inspection. `request id: infra-req-3141`

kevin: creating hardware ticket to replace GPU on node: https://infra.redwood/tickets/3141592 — noted ECC 423 corrected, thermal events, GPU reset Xid 79.

anna: good work. next steps:
- infra to RMA/replace GPU and run burn-in
- hardware team to run memory and thermal stress test (24h)
- create post-incident note with timeline and customer impact
- ML team to add protective fallback earlier in request pipeline for streaming tails (threshold at 1.2s queue)

devex: raising a small change to routing to prefer warm cached sessions on smaller quantized variants for long streams as an immediate cost-neutral fallback. PR draft: https://git.scm/redwood/pulls/8421

jess: customer reported degraded experience window narrowed to 07:09–07:18 UTC. asked if they'd like postmortem when ready.

customer-success: they want an RCA and mitigation summary. mark as follow-up deliverable.

ops_lead: tagging this P1 -> P1-> postmortem required. assign to anna (owner), raj (node investigation), kevin (hardware ticket), devex (fallback design). due 3 business days.

anna: acknowledged, will draft timeline and add logs. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated (traffic normalized). severity: P1 -> investigating (postmortem required). channels: #incidents #eng-runtime #eng-ml #customer-success

kevin: note for postmortem: include `nvidia-smi` ECC trending graph, kernel Xid resets, and streaming SDK retry behavior. recommend a follow-up to add automated quarantine when ECC single-bit errors exceed 100 in 6h.

raj: saving logs and artifacts:
- grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/snapshot/3141592654-snapshot
- kernel logs: gs://redwood-logs/prod/gpu-node-13/3141592654.tar.gz
- drain events: https://console.redwood/nodes/gpu-node-13/events

last: I'll open the postmortem doc and share a link when ready.

anna: last update before I hand off to PM: customer notified, node quarantined, p99 restored below SLO, replacement work scheduled. handing back to oncall rotation.

anna: handing to next oncall @kevin for overnight watch.

kevin: taking it. will monitor and coordinate with infra tomorrow morning.

(End of thread)
